top_choice_rationale: P001 is an original invention (the magic-wavelength lattice, Katori) demonstrated and then taken to the 10^-18 regime (Ye), independently reproduced at RIKEN/Tokyo, JILA, PTB, NIST and SYRTE, with a two-name allocation that is clean within the supplied names and a citation that can be worded around the lattice idea to stay distinct from the 2005 and 2012 prizes. P002 is a strong, mature second choice, but the 2D quantum spin Hall effect, the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang HgTe proposal and the separate 3D work make the three-name allocation harder to defend as the people who did the original work. Either is preferable to no award.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; only loose ties: Johansson is a Chalmers colleague (relevant to circuit QED, not on this slate), and I have microscopy exchanges with Japanese groups but no collaboration with Katori or Ye
